Cluster 0: Newer homes, moderately large, well-balanced with average 1959 year built, 4.4 rooms, 131.6 sqm, and high price per m2.
Cluster 1: Largest homes on average, 4.9 rooms, built around 1950, with price per m2 significantly lower than others.
Cluster 2: Smaller homes, more compact and efficient, with 3.9 rooms, built around 1957, and the highest price per m2.
Cluster 3: Older homes with slightly above-average size and rooms, built around 1946, with relatively low price per m2.
PC1 (Principal Component 1) is mainly influenced by changes since 1992, year, and price per m2 positively, while yield on mortgage credit bonds and nominal interest rate negatively affect it.
PC2 reflects geographic and regional variation, influenced positively by cluster, Zealand region, Capital area, and negatively by Jutland region and zip code.
The Stacking Regressor with Ridge as the final estimator achieved an RMSE of 988,454.82 and an R² score of 0.6309, indicating decent predictive performance on the housing price data.
